cards.title: Set up WooCommerce variable products with generated variations
cards.summary: Configure a variable product end-to-end: attributes, generated variations, per-variation SKU, price, stock and thumbnail.
cards.use_when: Adding a product that comes in multiple colors, sizes or other options on a WooCommerce store.
steps: Create the product and change Product type to 'Variable product' before saving.
In the Attributes tab add an attribute (e.g. Color), enter values separated by the pipe | symbol (white|blue|pink), tick 'Use for variations', and save attributes.
Open the Variations tab and click 'Generate variations' to auto-create one row per combination instead of adding them manually.
Edit each variation individually to set its own SKU (e.g. kova-echo-white), regular price, sale price, thumbnail and, if you manage stock per variation, stock quantity and low stock threshold.
Set the main Product image (the image shown before a shopper picks a variation) and add extra gallery images for the default color.
Publish, then preview the storefront and click through each option to confirm the image and price swap correctly per variation.
caveats: The specific button labels live in the WooCommerce product editor and can move between versions; verify the current interface.
Separate variations add admin overhead — don't generate variations for attributes that are purely descriptive.
cards.source_name: How to Create an Ecommerce Website with WordPress 2026 (step by step).docx

cards.title: Product data fields that drive PDP content: SKU, stock, weight
cards.summary: Fill WooCommerce Product Data tabs so stock messaging, shipping and descriptions match what the shopper sees.
cards.use_when: Creating or auditing a physical product listing on WooCommerce before it goes live.
steps: Set the SKU (your own stock-keeping code) and, if you have a real barcode, a UPC/GTIN. Skip barcodes for placeholder or made-up products.
Tick 'Track stock quantity' and enter the units on hand; set backorders to 'Do not allow' if you don't want to sell what you can't ship.
Set a low stock threshold (e.g. 10) so the product page can show 'low stock, order soon' messaging.
In the Shipping tab enter the weight and dimensions of the entire package — this is what shipping rates and label calculations use.
Write two descriptions: the long product description (the full sales story) and the short description (the summary that appears near the price/button).
Use the product image as the default PDP visual, a gallery for supporting shots, and category/tags so the item surfaces in on-site search and category browsing.
For downloadable or service products select Virtual/Downloadable instead of shipping fields.
caveats: Weight/dimensions are per package, not per item, when items ship together.
Low-stock and stock-count messages only show if you actually track inventory.
cards.source_name: How to Create an Ecommerce Website with WordPress 2026 (step by step).docx

cards.title: Configure Stripe and PayPal for WooCommerce and switch to live
cards.summary: Install payment plugins, connect accounts, run the connection test and flip the mode from Test to Live before launch.
cards.use_when: Enabling credit card and PayPal checkout on a WooCommerce store.
steps: Install and activate the Stripe and PayPal WooCommerce payment plugins from Plugins > Add New (search by name).
Open WooCommerce settings for Stripe, connect your Stripe account (business details, bank account, statement descriptor) and agree/submit.
With the account connected, change mode from Test to Live, run the connection test, and save.
Repeat the connection flow for PayPal, then go to WooCommerce > Settings > Payments and enable the PayPal gateway (it may be inactive by default).
Verify by adding a product to the cart, proceeding to checkout, and confirming both the card fields and the PayPal option appear.
caveats: Plugin names and settings screens change; verify current onboarding flow.
Do a live-mode test transaction before launch — the connection test confirms the link, not that checkout charges correctly.
The presenter is compensated via a hosting affiliate link; treat host recommendations as opinion.
cards.source_name: How to Create an Ecommerce Website with WordPress 2026 (step by step).docx

cards.title: Shipping zones, flat rate and free-shipping thresholds
cards.summary: Build shipping zones with a flat rate plus a free-shipping method gated by an order minimum, ordered so free shipping wins.
cards.use_when: Setting up shipping charges and a free-shipping minimum for an online store.
steps: In WooCommerce > Settings > Shipping create a zone per region (e.g. United States) and assign zone regions.
Add a Flat rate method: give it a name like 'Standard rate', set taxable status as appropriate, and enter a cost (example used: $10).
Add a Free shipping method and set its requirement to Minimum order amount (example threshold: $100). The operator can use any threshold; it must be chosen so shipping cost is covered.
Leave 'Apply minimum order rule before coupon' unchecked if the free-shipping threshold should be judged after coupons reduce the total.
Drag Free shipping above the flat rate inside the zone so qualifying carts get it automatically.
Save changes and test with a cart just above and just below the threshold.
caveats: The $100 threshold and $10 rate are the tutorial's examples, not benchmarks — margin and average order value should set your own numbers.
Local pickup is listed as rarely used; judge by whether customers can collect.
cards.source_name: How to Create an Ecommerce Website with WordPress 2026 (step by step).docx

cards.title: Welcome coupon setup: percentage, usage limits, exclusions
cards.summary: Create a first-order welcome coupon with a percentage discount and a one-use-per-customer limit.
cards.use_when: Launching a store or promo and you need a discount code that can't be abused.
steps: Go to WooCommerce > Marketing > Coupons and create a coupon with a simple code (e.g. welcome10).
Set discount type to Percentage and enter the value (example: 10).
Optionally tick 'free shipping' to bundle shipping into the coupon; skip it for the welcome case in the tutorial.
Set an expiration date, then under Usage restriction set minimum/maximum spend, prevent coupon stacking, exclude sale items, and scope to products/categories/brands if needed.
Under Usage limits set the per-user limit (example: 1) so each shopper can use it once, and optionally a total usage cap.
Publish, then test on the storefront by adding a product, applying the code in the cart, and confirming the discount amount.
caveats: Discount depth is a margin decision — the 10% example is illustrative, not a recommended rate.
Limits only work as configured; verify the per-user rule actually blocks a second redemption.
cards.source_name: How to Create an Ecommerce Website with WordPress 2026 (step by step).docx

cards.title: Use a starter template, then customize instead of building from scratch
cards.summary: Install a theme plus starter templates and Elementor so a full store layout exists before you customize.
cards.use_when: Building a new WordPress/WooCommerce storefront and you want a working layout fast.
steps: Install and activate a lightweight theme (Astra is used in the tutorial), then launch its starter-templates plugin.
When choosing templates, click back before proceeding and explicitly select Elementor as the page builder — the tutorial warns against the block editor for this workflow.
Filter templates by Ecommerce, pick a free one (premium tags are paid), and let the importer install the pages, Elementor and WooCommerce.
Logo, font and color choices at import are placeholders — the presenter says they get replaced later, so don't over-invest there.
After import, use 'Edit with Elementor' on the homepage and replace text, images and backgrounds section by section rather than rebuilding.
caveats: Imported templates include demo products and categories (e.g. 'Indoor plants') that must be deleted.
Template import writes many pages/settings; check for leftover demo content before launch.
cards.source_name: How to Create an Ecommerce Website with WordPress 2026 (step by step).docx

cards.title: Elementor structure: sections, containers and widgets
cards.summary: Understand the three-level Elementor hierarchy and how to build a hero section from an empty canvas.
cards.use_when: Editing the homepage or a landing page in Elementor and you need to control layout and positioning.
steps: Treat the page as sections (full-width background bands, shown by the pink outline), containers inside them (gray dashed boxes), and widgets/elements inside containers.
Add a section with the plus button, pick Flexbox, and choose a column/container arrangement; templates or AI-generated layouts are alternative starting points.
To make a section fill the screen, select the container's six-dot handle, change minimum height units to VH and drag the slider to 100.
Drag widgets in from the element panel (Heading, Text Editor, Divider, Button, Image, Icon Box) and edit text either in the sidebar field or directly on canvas.
Center content vertically with the container's Justify Content setting.
Reorder by dragging sections on canvas or by dragging entries in the structure/layers panel.
Preview without editing outlines using the preview arrow, then publish to save.
caveats: Newer Elementor versions default to containers rather than the older section/column model; verify the current editor.
Two-height, viewport-sized sections can behave differently on mobile until you set responsive padding.
cards.source_name: How to Create an Ecommerce Website with WordPress 2026 (step by step).docx

cards.title: Style buttons for visibility: normal vs hover states, padding, radius
cards.summary: Configure button normal and hover states, padding and border radius so the CTA stands out on the page.
cards.use_when: Designing add-to-cart or buy-now buttons on a homepage, landing page or product page.
steps: Select the button widget and open Style; note there are separate Normal and Hover tabs — set both.
Set text color and background (classic solid color or gradient) for Normal; set a clearly different text and background for Hover so the change is obvious to shoppers.
Optionally apply a hover animation such as 'Grow' to draw attention to the CTA.
Control shape with Border Radius: 0 gives a square button, higher values approach a circle; the tutorial lands mid-range (~15).
Control size with Padding; unlink the four values when you want wide but not tall buttons (example: 32 left/right, 15 top/bottom).
Keep button padding and label short enough that the button doesn't read as a large box on mobile.
caveats: These are styling levers, not proven conversion lifts — validate any change against your own analytics.
Hover states don't exist on touch devices, so don't rely on hover alone to signal interactivity.
cards.source_name: How to Create an Ecommerce Website with WordPress 2026 (step by step).docx

cards.title: Video and image hero sections on the homepage
cards.summary: Use an Elementor section with a video or gradient background, then fix contrast so overlaid text stays readable.
cards.use_when: Building or replacing the homepage hero that showcases a top product.
steps: Select the hero section's six-dot handle, open Style > Background, and choose Classic (solid), Gradient, or the Video tab.
For video, host it (the tutorial uses an unlisted YouTube video) and paste the link into the video URL field.
Add a subtle gradient overlay or choose text colors that contrast with the moving background.
After adding the video, change text to white (or a contrasting color) in Style > Text Color for each heading and paragraph, since overlaying copy on video can obscure it.
Swap individual elements freely: duplicate a heading to create a subheading, adjust typography weight and size, and add a Divider at reduced width to separate content.
Use an Image widget for product visuals where video is not appropriate.
caveats: Background video typically will not autoplay on mobile and can look broken — plan a mobile-specific alternative (see responsive card).
Only use media you have the rights to host.
cards.source_name: How to Create an Ecommerce Website with WordPress 2026 (step by step).docx

cards.title: Header and footer are theme settings, not Elementor
cards.summary: Edit the Astra header via Customize (logo, menu, transparent header) while page content stays in Elementor.
cards.use_when: Changing the store logo, navigation menu or header background color.
steps: Open Customize from the admin bar — this controls the theme header and footer, which Elementor does not manage.
Replace the logo: untoggle the separate transparent logo option so one logo is used sitewide, then upload a transparent PNG and set the logo width (skip cropping so the image isn't cut).
Set the site title, which is what appears in the browser tab.
Enable a transparent header on the complete website, and uncheck it for WooCommerce product pages if you want the same header on PDPs.
Adjust header background under Design > Primary Header: choose a color (e.g. black) and reduce the slider to about half opacity for a translucent header.

Edit the navigation menu via the pencil icon > Configure Menu > Primary Menu: add Pages, Custom Links, Posts, Products or product categories, and drag items sideways under another item to create dropdown sub-items.
Set menu text/link color and hover color under Transparent Header > Design to match the site's palette.
Publish.
caveats: Theme options and labels shift between Astra versions; verify the current Customizer panels.
Changing header colors may require updating body-section text colors for contrast.
cards.source_name: How to Create an Ecommerce Website with WordPress 2026 (step by step).docx

cards.title: Organize the catalog with product categories and parent/child structure
cards.summary: Create product categories (and parents) so shoppers can sort and categories surface on the homepage.
cards.use_when: Organizing a WooCommerce product catalog into navigable categories and subcategories before building collection menus and homepage sections.
steps: Go to Products > Categories and delete demo categories that shipped with the template (e.g. 'Indoor plants').
Add a new category with a clear name, a simple lowercase slug for the URL, and optionally a parent category.
Use parent categories to group variants, e.g. put 'Wireless headphones' and 'Earbuds' under a parent 'Headphones'.
Skip thumbnail/description for now if they aren't ready — they can be added later.
Assign each product to the right category in the product editor (and uncheck Uncategorized) so it appears in that category's listings and the homepage sections that pull from it.
Add tags to products to help on-site search, using your own brand or product name as tags.
caveats: Categories are what on-site browsing and menu dropdowns rely on; tags help search but shouldn't replace categories.
A flat, one-level category set is fine for small catalogs — the tutorial starts that way.
cards.source_name: How to Create an Ecommerce Website with WordPress 2026 (step by step).docx

cards.title: Upsells and cross-sells in WooCommerce linked products
cards.summary: Use WooCommerce Linked Products so shoppers see an upgrade on the product page and add-ons in the cart.
cards.use_when: Setting product recommendations on a PDP and in the cart to raise average order value.
steps: In the product editor's Linked Products tab, add Upsells — these show on the product page as an upgraded or higher-priced alternative to the item being viewed.
Add Cross-sells — these appear in the cart when the shopper is close to checking out.
Search for the products by name in each field; the targets must already exist as products in the store.
Keep the relationship relevant (related product, not a random item) so the recommendation makes sense.
Review on the storefront: open a PDP to see upsells and add an item to cart to see cross-sells render.
caveats: Recommending unrelated items can distract from checkout; the tutorial's example pairs a cheaper headphone with a nicer one, not an arbitrary product.
Cross-sells add cart steps — measure whether they help or hurt checkout completion.
cards.source_name: How to Create an Ecommerce Website with WordPress 2026 (step by step).docx

cards.title: Clean up demo products before adding your own catalog
cards.summary: Delete template products and their trash, then replicate a configured product for the rest of the catalog instead of rebuilding each one.
cards.use_when: Starting a store from an imported template and needing to replace placeholder products.
steps: Go to Products > All Products, select all demo products, apply the 'Move to trash' bulk action, then empty the trash.
With an empty catalog, the 'Add product' flow prompts for product type: Physical (shipped), Variable (has variations like color/size), Grouped (a bundle sold as one).
Reuse the structure: duplicate an existing configured product and edit it for the next item rather than repeating every field from scratch.
Confirm new items appear in the homepage product sections that reference the catalog, and assign each to its category and price.
If product thumbnails look grainy in grids, change the product image size in Customizer to e.g. 900x600 and republish.
caveats: Duplicating carries over old images, descriptions and variations — scrub those before publishing.
Image-size values are examples from the tutorial, not measured optimal sizes.
cards.source_name: How to Create an Ecommerce Website with WordPress 2026 (step by step).docx

cards.title: Responsive design: serve different sections per device in Elementor
cards.summary: Duplicate a desktop section and use Elementor's responsive controls to show a simplified version only on mobile.
cards.use_when: Fixing the homepage on mobile/tablet, e.g. a background video that doesn't play on phones.
steps: Switch to the phone/tablet icon in Elementor's responsive preview and inspect the section — video backgrounds often render as a gray gap on mobile.
Duplicate the desktop hero section so you have two copies.
On the duplicate meant for mobile, open Advanced > Responsive and hide it on tablet and desktop, leaving mobile enabled.
On the original desktop section, hide it on mobile and leave tablet/desktop enabled, so each device sees one clean version.
In the mobile section, remove the video link (or leave it blank), set the background to a gradient, and add a product Image widget instead.
Use Advanced > Padding with the mobile-only indicator to space the section and keep content clear of the header; adjust per-element mobile settings like button position.
Preview each device view before publishing.
caveats: Duplicated sections multiply maintenance — update both when content changes.
Pixel values shown are illustrative; check across real devices.
cards.source_name: How to Create an Ecommerce Website with WordPress 2026 (step by step).docx

cards.title: Single product page spacing and button styling via Customize
cards.summary: Fix PDP padding and recolor add-to-cart buttons in the Customizer rather than in Elementor.
cards.use_when: Adjusting layout and colors on the WooCommerce product page so content clears the header and CTAs match the brand.
steps: Open the single product page and click Customize to reach the WooCommerce Single Product settings (these are theme options, not Elementor).
Under Single Product > Design, unlink the padding values and set top padding (example: 120px) so the content clears the sticky header.
Change the sticky add-to-cart button colors (background and hover) under the same Design panel; a page refresh may be needed for updates to show.
Change global button background/hover under Global > Buttons, then publish and refresh to confirm.
Edit the shipping-note text on the PDP (e.g. 'free shipping') under General > Single Product if your shipping terms differ.
Add a purchase note under the product's Advanced tab for a custom post-purchase message, and keep menu order at 0 unless you need manual sorting.
caveats: Setting padding without checking the responsive views can push content off small screens.
Customizer labels vary by theme version.
cards.source_name: How to Create an Ecommerce Website with WordPress 2026 (step by step).docx
